page.layout: One page of running text in one column, no margin notes. Below the text: signature "Z 3" at the left and catchword "nes" at the right.

main_text.p: linguam maternam hodie vocari. Tu qui omnia scis, & me Mercurio opus non habes, vocas linguam vernaculam radicaliter, & oppositè. illo modo linguam Græcorum veterum hodie in Sacris vsitata vernacula vocatur, quia in Græcia orta, & nata est, in Græcia vsurpata, legibus, consuetudine a multis introducta seculis; sed iniuria temporis, & desidia hominum, qui quod tueri mascule debuissent, turpiter neglexerunt. μακάριε τῶ ϑεοπνεύστῳ. Tu ita vocas linguam vernaculam contra atque alij. Eris ne ergo tu auctor linguæ pro arbitrio inuertens, atque immutans omnia? Quare & Lexicon non conscribis, vt omnibus pateat, ista tua noua verborum significatio? Græca lingua in Græcia orta est. plane. in Græcia vsurpata saltem per multa tempora. Sed cum tempore omnia vertantur, & immutentur in peiorem partem, lingua quoque ab illa pura, & primigenia aliam, atque aliam faciem induit nunc elegantiorem, nunc deformiorem; donec deducta est, vt in communibus colloquijs, & familiaribus congressibus in vsu fit. & vernæ etiam & homines nihili eam vsurpent, ita disiunctam, & diuersam ab illa prima, vt primam illam homines pauci, & linguarum studiosi, nec non musarum alumni intelligant, hanc sine literis homi-

page.notes: The Greek phrase "μακάριε τῶ ϑεοπνεύστῳ" is only partly legible at this scan resolution; the letters are copied as seen, without certainty. "oppositè" is italic and its final accent is doubtful. The word "vsurpata" in the phrase "in Græcia vsurpata, legibus" and the italic status of "vernacula" in "in Sacris vsitata vernacula" are uncertain. The line-end "homi-" is a printed hyphen, and the catchword "nes" completes it.
